messages:
raquel: Heads-up — saw a regression on master for multi-GPU decode after the quant-routing change. Comm/compute overlap drops and allreduce tail latency spikes during steady-state.

mike: Which commit and config?

raquel: commit `8f3a2b` (runtime: quant-routing v2). Test: 4xA100, TP=2 PP=2, seq=1024, batch=8. Before: allreduce tail ~1.2ms. After: spikes to 8-10ms and GPUs have idle gaps during token loop.

tori: Any traces (nvtx/nvprof)? Could be streams getting serialized or cuGraph replays forcing host syncs.

raquel: Pasting condensed trace and perf summary: 
```
[perf-summary]
model: gptq-13b
commit: 8f3a2b
gpus: 4xA100
tp:2 pp:2
before: 1.2ms allreduce tail / 98% overlap
after: 8.4ms allreduce tail / 42% overlap
observed: SM idle intervals during decode loop
```

```
# nvprof excerpt
GPU0: kernel decode_kv_q (stream 5) 0.4ms
GPU0: kernel matmul_fused (stream 7) 1.1ms
GPU0: ncclAllReduce (stream 7) 7.9ms wait
GPU0: cudagraph replay (stream 3) host sync
```

henry: That NCCL time is suspicious. Maybe the kernel selector assigned fallback kernels to a legacy/global stream and we end up with mixed-stream capture/replay ordering. If decode writes KV on one stream and the graph expects another, replay will synchronize.

tori: I remember the quant-route added a fallback path that does a `cudaStreamSynchronize()` in cold path for correctness. If that happens during steady-state, it kills overlap.

raquel: I grepped the selector: when `quantized_flag && short_seq_opt` -> route to fallback kernels. Fallback currently binds to `stream-0` and posts host sync to be cuGraph-friendly. Old path used per-worker graph streams and async NCCL.

mike: Can you share the stream assignments? Also the scheduler diff.

raquel: Stream map snippet:
```
KV prefetch -> stream 2 (per-gpu)
Decode kernels -> stream 5
Compute kernels -> stream 7
CuGraph replay -> stream 3 (per-worker graph stream)
Allreduce -> stream 7 (NCCL)
Fallback kernels (quant-route) -> stream 0 + host sync
```

henry: Ok there's the mismatch. Fallback using stream 0 + host sync will stall the host thread and break our pipelining. Why is fallback using stream 0 instead of the worker graph stream?

tori: In the refactor the fallback re-used the legacy stream pool to avoid touching capture code. That means captures and replays can be on different streams and replay forces a host sync. Oops.

raquel: Repro note: regression only triggers when KV cache prefetch concurrently interacts with the quantized fallback path. If I disable KV prefetch, overlap returns to normal. So it's a cross-stream ordering edge case.

mike: Short-term mitigation: bind fallback to the per-worker graph stream and remove the host sync. Open a quick PR and run perf CI.

perf-bot: perf regression alert: compare/master -> HEAD. 95th latency increased 6.8x on multi-gpu decode. Diff profile: more host sync events in cuGraph replay. https://perf.internal/runs/233450-quant-route

raquel: Proposed fix: 1) fallback uses per-worker graph stream; 2) add debug assert if fallback binds global stream; 3) add lightweight integration test capturing a mixed path to catch host syncs.

henry: Also add a runtime heuristic: if fallback occurs during steady-state, prefer the active capture/graph stream for issuing kernels. Add code comments documenting capture/stream invariants.

tori: I'll run triangle tests: reproduce on 2xA100 then 4/8. Test matrix: KV prefetch ON/OFF, quant-route toggled.

mike: PR #4129 opened — quick patch to bind fallback to worker graph stream and remove explicit sync. CI perf running.

raquel: Local perf shows overlap back to ~92% and allreduce tail ~1.4ms.

tori: If CI perf agrees, backport to release. Also add an integration test that simulates occasional fallback during capture to prevent regressions.

mike: Agreed. We'll also audit other usages of the legacy stream pool to find more mismatches.

raquel: Adding capture-path debug logs to surface when fallbacks bind to non-graph streams so perf runs can catch earlier. :seedling:

perf-bot: CI perf results for branch #4129 — multi-GPU restore within noise, no single-GPU regressions.

mike: Nice work, ship after reviews. :shipit:
